title: Ai game hate
author: ZookeepergameNo3091
selftext: So I posted about my early stage game ”Armory Ascend” in a few dev groups on Reddit. Goal being lifting a total of 1000$ to finish the game and cover costs, but so far every comment has been about the use of Ai. I’m very clear about the use of Ai in my kickstarter and using Ai as a tool is the reason I can make this game free after launch (to cut down costs and save time as a non-fulltime dev) Here’s the video I posted with some gameplay. Now I have to ask, why are people so mad at AI games? Personally, as long as the game is entertaining and ai usage clear I couldn’t care less if it created by ai. Please use this post to discuss this topic in general!

comments.author: Almaravarion
comments.body:
My personal take on that, and take it from someone who is actively using AI in prototyping right now:

I don't think people are mad at AI itself, but at the influx of 'just-another-remake-of-popular-games' with varying levels of quality, flooding the market right now, and drowning storefronts with remake of remakes of remakes.

And yes, that would include Your game, which is yet another remake of Vampire survivors in just-another visual theme.

replies.author: ZookeepergameNo3091
replies.body: And I get that take honestly, but the thing is it’s not really a ”copy” of vampire survivors is it? It’s a wave based game sure, lots of games did similar stuff before vampire survivors, I’m truly not trying to copy the game itself. Similarities does not mean copying does it? There’s bosses, a unique forging system, multiple characters with different playstyles, shops etc

replies.body: The only difference you could come up with is the "unique forging system"... so yeaht it's just another clone.

replies.author: Almaravarion
replies.body:
Trailer shows one - generating new random looks for randomly generated weapons; Hardly a groundbreaking tech really.

The reason why most people, me included, listed Vampire Survivors, is that while not exactly the first of bullet-heaven style gameplay, it was one of the bigger hits on mobile, pushing the genre into popularity, and spawning countless 'survivor' title games and effectively coining survivor-like as a genre.

Out of bosses? Present in VS, Unique forging system - that's one that I didn't see. Multiple characters with different playstyles? Present in VS, playstyle coming from minor adjustments though, no playstyle difference shown in trailer. Shops? Take a wild fucking guess if they are present in VS or other survivor style games.

The only thing that is unique here is generating new image for every 'newly forged' weapon, which themselves are apparently mostly RNG based stats, rather than actually unique in gameplay. Nothing that other games haven't done before.

replies.author: olafthemanofsnow
replies.body:
And that final comment is where the problem lies. You have had an idea, but haven't done any planning. One of the first things I do when I start the design work on anything is plan, which includes competitor research. Is my idea uniquely different to what already exists? And i would spend days and weeks working that out before a single prompt. 

I personally dont play this type of game, but for any genre, and especially in an AI era when everyone has access to tools, you need to be a level above. To understand game design, your target audience, consumer behaviour, marketing. You cant just reskin something and hope. 

If you want you can buy my course....just kidding.

comments.author: askdoobie
comments.body:
The problem is, this looks like a game a friend of mine made in three days with Gemini Flash 3.8. It looks low-effort. When you have a game, you need to promote the character, tell a story, and feature good graphics. Show the gameplay. What makes your game different? You have three seconds to get the first good point across. 

With AI, people want you to be sick at making games. AI is not an excuse for bad quality. There is no excuse anymore for bad quality. You need to show AAA quality when using AI; then people will be more accepting of it.

  
A game is not just mechanics, it's emotional attachment. Make something people can love.

replies.author: ZookeepergameNo3091

Adding a very AI-slop-looking shop doesn't have enough of an impact on the gameplay to stop me from calling it yet another Vampire Survivors clone.

comments.author: ganJscopez
comments.body: How did you explain the $1k required costs in your posts because you didn't explain them here. That's a pretty important distinction, since nobody else who is vibe-coding games needs a kickstarter for money and your game doesn't look like anything special among the sea of AI-prototypes that people are making and releasing without kickstarter already.

replies.author: ZookeepergameNo3091
replies.body: That’s a fair point, I might’ve been unclear how exactly this money would’ve been used. However many people ”vibe-coding” are going to make money of their game, I’m not, I just want to cover the costs and release an ad free game for free.

replies.author: ganJscopez
replies.body:
Yeah I guess that's true, although 99% of those games will never even make the $300 steam fee back so in that case you will already be way ahead in profits in comparison to them if your kickstarter were to work out in the end. But in general $1k sounds like a lot to ask for a AI-coded game that you're working for fun on the side. It's going to be a real tough sell even for people who don't mind AI,. Before even attempting to go the kickstarter route, you would definitely want to have more work / potential to show off before someone would want to go so far as to sign up on kickstarter and fill in their details to send you money with no guarantee of returns (TONS of kickstarter games simply get abandoned).

If you want money, make the game and sell it. If you want it to be F2P, don't ask for money and just finish it with the monthly subs like everyone else. Good luck brotha.

replies.author: ZookeepergameNo3091
replies.body: Yeah that’s fair, but I thought kickstarter basically says ”finish the game or pay back the money”. I’m not super familiar with kickstarter in itself

comments.author: Material-Database-24
comments.body:
In general, the bigger problem is that some AI devs come forward like 5yo come fwd with their stick drawing of their family, and expect the same reaction from public as their mum had towards it. Putting ones work out on public means it will draw in the critics. It's part of the game, be it AI or not involved, so one kinda needs to accept that critique, and let it be, and continue on their own way.

For AI game to sell for tough gaming audience, it needs to show higher quality than average hobbyist game and/or new novel approach over typical game in that genre.

I see here couple issues that will draw extra negative attitude: 1) the game is not novel, 2) the shown quality is obvious AI, and 3) you come up front seeking for money to finish it, especially due 1 and 2.

It's hard reality that your game will be tough to sell. It would be that even if made without AI. The money aspect will amplify the negativity, as people will find it "low effort bait" to try make money, although no-one is forcing them to do anything. It's kinda same as printing a stock photo, framing it, and asking 200 for it. It will draw people to ridicule it, even if there's nothing in particular wrong with it.

replies.author: ZookeepergameNo3091
replies.body: Thank you for a detailed comment! I do truly get this and when you put it like that it does seem ridiculous. The only reason I thought it would be fair to ask for funding to finish the game is because I didn’t want to make any money of the game itself, keeping it ad free, but if I myself pull 1000$ from my own pocket to finish and post a game for the world for free, that just doesn’t make sense. Honestly I’ll probably just have to set a cost to the game so I won’t have to ask for funding in the first place

replies.author: Material-Database-24
replies.body:
My suggestion is, concentrate next on the animations. I do not play games like this, but those that do, can definitely appreciate it, when it is fun to play and cool to look at.

So make it look "polished" and you'll likely get way better response. Make a free demo, and set price of full game reasonable. It might draw enough enthusiasts to give you more back than invested.

After all, be it AI or not, when the game is built with passion and dedication, polished, and is actually fun to play and looks "good", it will draw in the correct kinda audience and no-one cares if its AI or not.

replies.author: ZookeepergameNo3091
replies.body: Thanks for  the suggestion, I’ll keep it in mind
